rule.description: The Redis client flavor detection (the node-redis sharded-capability probe `typeof <client>.sSubscribe === "function"`) and the per-flavor sharded publish/subscribe command dispatch (sSubscribe/sUnsubscribe/sPublish vs ssubscribe/sunsubscribe/spublish, together with the legacy smessageBuffer channel->handler registry) must be owned by one shared compatibility location; re-implementing them inline at several sites scatters one responsibility so that a conceptual compatibility change requires coordinated edits everywhere.

checks.description: Detect functions that re-implement the node-redis client flavor detection inline (`typeof <client>.sSubscribe === "function"`) instead of consulting a single shared detection helper; the relation is duplicated when more than one function performs the detection.
checks.detected_relation: function -> inline duplicated client flavor detection
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: One conceptual decision (which Redis client flavor is connected) is re-derived site by site, so changing detection or adding a client package requires editing every copy in step.

matches.evidence: The single surviving detection helper; after the scattering it is consulted only by the server-count polling path while every other flavor-dependent site re-derives the detection locally, so this location becomes one member of a duplicated relation rather than the owner.
The standard adapter's subscription setup re-checks the client flavor with a locally duplicated capability probe (drifted to the sharded-capability spelling) instead of a shared detection.
The standard adapter's teardown re-checks the client flavor with a second local copy of the same capability probe.
Both the main-channel and the response-channel subscription blocks embed their own copy of the flavor probe and the matching per-flavor command branch and listener-registry setup.
Dynamic room subscription re-implements the flavor probe and subscribe dispatch locally in its own copy.
Dynamic room unsubscribe re-implements the flavor probe and unsubscribe dispatch locally.
Adapter teardown probes the client flavor again inside its per-channel unsubscribe loop and selects the command spelling inline.
The broadcast publish path probes the publishing client with another local copy of the flavor detection before choosing the publish command spelling.
The response publish path carries yet another local copy of the flavor probe and the per-flavor publish branch.

checks.description: Detect functions that issue the per-flavor dispatch of a sharded Pub/Sub command directly (both the node-redis camelCase spelling and the legacy lowercase spelling, plus the legacy smessageBuffer registry handling); a command family's dispatch is duplicated when more than one function implements it.
checks.detected_relation: function -> inline duplicated per-flavor sharded command dispatch
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Issuing one sharded command correctly per client flavor (command casing, buffer flags, registry bookkeeping, promise shape) is one responsibility; implementing it at several sites forces the same coordinated edit at all of them whenever a client package changes.

matches.evidence: Subscribes the main and response channels by directly branching on the client flavor and issuing sSubscribe/ssubscribe with registry setup, re-implementing the subscribe dispatch twice inline.
Re-implements the same per-flavor subscribe dispatch (including its own listener-registry setup) for dynamically created room channels.
Re-implements the per-flavor unsubscribe dispatch locally for deleted room channels, including registry cleanup.
Re-implements the per-flavor unsubscribe dispatch inside the teardown loop over all subscribed channels, including registry cleanup.
Issues the broadcast publish directly through a per-flavor branch, re-implementing the publish dispatch for the message path.
Issues the response publish directly through the same kind of per-flavor branch, duplicating the publish dispatch a second time.

excluded: lib/util.ts PUBSUB: cluster-flavor detection inside the server-count command (constructor.name/isCluster/masters shape checks) stays centralized and is intentionally outside this rule; both adapters' serverCount() paths keep calling PUBSUB, so counting is not a scattered responsibility in this case.

Standard Pub/Sub command issuance in lib/index.ts (psubscribe/psubscribe callbacks, publish): the lowercase spellings are accepted by every supported client, so there is no per-flavor command dispatch to scatter there; only the flavor-probe copies at the setup/teardown gates are part of the smell.

Message encode/decode decision logic (the 0x7b JSON peek and hasBinary-based msgpack selection) is a wire-format concern, a different responsibility from client-flavor command dispatch, and is not credited.
Request/response correlation state and timeouts in the standard adapter (requests/ackRequests maps) are untouched by the injected scattering and are not credited.
